I originally thought that this bug only impacted the OpenTUI interface.
But from my testing OpenCode web is also impacted.
Response times for simple prompts that would typically take seconds, often take minutes.
I haven't fully confirmed this, but it seemed like it was wasting tokens with more requests.
It could be dangerous, even if you were on the cusp, as you would likely not even notice you are spending x% more unneeded tokens.

The fix provided above fixed OpenCode web for me.

It is also worth noting that if https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/775 made it into release, it did not fix the issue.
The last version I tested on was [v1.3.8](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.3.8).

Update: Dug into this on my local opencode fork (updated to `dev` tip at post time) and my issue seems to have a different root cause from the ones discussed above.

In my case, sessions all shared the same git-derived `project_id`, but `/sessions` backend (and the Sessions dialog) was still hiding most of them because it was filtering by exact `session.directory`. I had 77 session rows split across four paths (`opencode`, `opencode-cli`, `opencode/packages/opencode`, `opencode-cli.bak`) due to local repo/folder renames.

After normalising them all to the correct directory, every missing session came back. So at least for me, this wasn't the 100-session limit or the 30-day filter. Exact directory scoping was independently dropping sessions even when the `project_id` matched.

This looks like an interaction between `b020758` (show all project sessions from any working directory), `68bb8ce` (database-level session filtering), and `c7760b4` (SDK rewrite that sends `directory` on `/session` requests).

Hey, I was testing kiro locally and found a few issues with why it doesn't show up in the TUI.

Repro: Complete kiro OAuth login (~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json exists, token valid) → launch TUI → kiro missing from model selection and "Connect provider" dialog.

Root causes:
1. discoverModels() uses POST, but API only supports GET: discoverModels() calls POST listAvailableModels, but the actual API only accepts GET ListAvailableModels?origin=AI_EDITOR. POST returns 400 UnknownOperationException → 0 models → provider gets deleted.
2. Custom loader skips kiro because it's not in models.dev: The CUSTOM_LOADERS loop checks database[providerID] and does continue if not found. Since kiro has no models.dev entry, the custom loader never runs. And even if it did, mergeProvider also silently drops providers missing from the database.
3. Discovery loop is hardcoded to gitlab only: kiro's discoverModels gets registered in discoveryLoaders but the actual invocation only runs for gitlab. Kiro's discovery never executes.

Fixes needed in provider.ts:
- discoverModels(): POST → GET, fix URL path/params, update response type mapping
- Custom loader loop: create a fallback empty provider when not in database, and let mergeProvider register it
- Discovery loop: iterate all discoveryLoaders instead of hardcoding gitlab
Adding kiro to models.dev (your other PR) fixes 2, but 1 and 3 are still needed for dynamic model discovery to work.

Hi @kitlangton, noticed this PR is still in draft — wanted to flag a related timing issue we've been investigating that might be worth considering as part of this refactor.
We traced a bug (#20026) where plugin providers registered via the config() hook disappear after /instance/dispose. The root cause is that configProviders = Object.entries(cfg.provider ?? {}) is captured as a stale snapshot before plugin.list() runs and calls the config() hook. When plugins modify cfg.provider to add their providers, it's already too late.
Your refactor injects dep (with auth and config bridges) into custom loaders, which is a nice improvement — but it doesn't address the ordering of plugin.list() relative to configProviders.
Since this PR is still in draft, would you be open to proposing a solution that also addresses the initialization ordering? We have a fix in PR #20777 that moves plugin.list() to run before configProviders, but we'd be happy to see a more elegant approach from you if you think it fits better into this refactor.
Happy to collaborate or adjust our approach if you have ideas.
